title: the autopilot finishes the self project's merge path without hand scripts: it builds merge card details from the answered dispatch card when none are authored, and wakes once for a draft pull request
acceptance: Why. The captain (2026-10-07) reviewed which firstmate habits live only in memory and answered verbatim: "好 先B再C 其他照你的意思改", approving that rules become code first. All day firstmate ran its merge path by hand with untracked local scripts (review wait, CI wait, a merge-card lock, update-branch, a coverage count, fm-gate, the merge-card request). Those scripts matched their own wrapper process, miscounted suites and left a stale lock. The autopilot (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py) already owns the same path on origin/main 4d4374f: gates, review launch on gate 6, the merge lock, base and head checks, and the merge-card request at :470-510. What it lacks is why the hand scripts existed: it stops at :503-507 with a wake whenever no merge-card details file exists, and it returns silently for a draft pull request at :286. This task closes those two gaps for the self project so firstmate needs no hand chain. Network stall timeouts belong to T-253, and a rerun rule for known flaky tests is a later task; this task touches neither.

Change 1, merge-card details from the dispatch card (new bin/lib/fm_merge_details.py, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py). `build(state, project, task, pr_number)` runs for the self project only (external projects, which can carry a not-runnable fail-first gate from T-240 and do not reload the board on merge, keep today's wake with the reason "external project: author the details"). It reads, among the answered decisions for the task whose purpose is dispatch and whose chosen option is A, the one with the highest `<n>` (state/decisions/D-<project>-<task key>-<n>.json; its `details` holds the en and zh-TW intent-card fields), and returns merge-card details with the same contract fm-decide.sh --kind merge checks today (design :430-438): every intent field copied (intent, why, scope_in, scope_out, done, notes, before_nodes, after_nodes); `done` gains a first item "CI, review and the six gates are green on this head." / "這個 head 的 CI、審查和六關全綠。"; `title` is "MERGE CARD — merge PR #<n>: " plus the dispatch title without its leading "Dispatch <task>: " when that prefix is present, else the whole dispatch title (zh-TW "【合併卡】合併 PR #<n>：" plus the dispatch title without "派工 <task>：" when present, else the whole title); `explanation` is "The review approved <task>. CI, coverage and the six gates must be green on this head before you see this card." (zh-TW "審查核准了 <task>。這個 head 的 CI、覆蓋檢查和六關都必須全綠。"); `before` and `after` are copied from the dispatch card in each locale; `outcome` "Option A merges only PR #<n>. The board then replaces itself on the new code." (zh-TW "選項 A 只合併 PR #<n>。之後看板自己換上新程式。"); options: A with description "Merge #<n>" (zh-TW "合併 #<n>") and the dispatch card's A pros and cons; B with description "Hold the merge" (zh-TW "暫緩合併"), pros "The code stays the same." (zh-TW "程式維持原樣。") and the dispatch card's B cons; C with description "Ask for a fix" (zh-TW "要求修正"), pros "You can change the scope." (zh-TW "你可以改範圍。") and cons "A change needs a new review, CI and six gates." (zh-TW "修改需要重新審查、CI 和六關。"); every fixed sentence here passes `fm_ste` (checked on base); `questions` = the dispatch card's questions when present, else one fact "The change stays inside the pinned scope." / "改動不超出固定的範圍。"; `change_table` = one row whose text is the first intent item, A ✓, B —, C —. It then runs `fm_ste` check-details with kind merge on the result, which also covers the fields fm-decide.sh --request requires (bin/fm-decide.sh:385-395). In merge_card at :503-507, when the authored file state/decision-details/<id>.json is missing, the autopilot calls build and writes the result to state/decision-details-built/<id>.json, a directory outside the inputs that the advance fingerprint reads (:297-310 globs only state/decision-details/), so writing it or a failed --request never changes the fingerprint and never starts another gate run; it then passes that path to fm-decide.sh --request --details. The authored file, when present, always wins and is never overwritten. When build cannot produce a passing file, the wake keeps its existing prefix "<task> ready: merge card details needed (<id>)" and adds the reason: "no answered dispatch card", the checker's structural error text (for example a dispatch card without intent fields, a `done` list that would exceed its limit, or locale count mismatches; fm_ste raises ValueError for these), or the failing STE lines.

Change 2, draft pull requests (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py). In advance at :286, a draft pull request of any project that has no running job for the task queues one wake per head through `queue` with identity `draft-<n>-<head>`: "<task> #<n> is a draft at <head12>: the merge path waits; mark it ready" / zh-TW "<task> #<n> 仍是草稿：合併流程在等待，請標成 ready", then returns as today. tests/lib/autopilot_task_resolution.py drives draft pull requests through this branch: the assertions at :119, :124, :130, :133, :135, :141, :143 and :170 (test_answered_ask_and_wrong_head_never_wake, whose draft now reaches :286) add the expected `draft-<n>-<head>` identity; the upgrade-test assertions at :157, :160 and :163 return before the draft check and stay as they are; no other change. It never marks a pull request ready itself. The worker is unchanged; a later task can make a finished round mark its own draft ready. On the first poll after this lands, each open draft pull request gets one wake.

Not changed, stated. Red CI handling, including reruns of flaky tests (a later task); network timeouts (T-253); the gate list, the merge lock and its blocker, the order of gates and review, the captain's click as the only merge, fm-decide's validation, external projects' handling of red CI, and authored merge-card details.

Tests, new behaviour (each fails on the base commit and passes after). New tests/autopilot-merge-path.test.sh (committed executable) running tests/lib/autopilot_merge_path.py with the existing autopilot fixtures, with gh stubs that answer like real gh JSON: (1) self project, gates green, no details file, an answered dispatch card: state/decision-details-built/<id>.json appears with the merge title, the done first item and all intent fields, and fm-decide --request runs once with that path; (2) after (1), a second poll with unchanged inputs starts no new gate job; (3) two answered dispatch cards: the one with the higher <n> is used; (4) a dispatch title without the "Dispatch <task>: " prefix: the merge title carries the whole title; (5) a dispatch card whose zh-TW text fails STE: no built file, the wake names the failing line; (6) a dispatch card without intent fields: no built file, the wake carries the checker's field error; (7) no dispatch card: no built file, the wake says so; (8) an external project with gates green and no authored details: no built file, the wake names the external reason; (9) a draft pull request with no running job queues one wake per head and none on a second poll.

Tests, regression (pass on base and after). An authored details file is used unchanged and is never overwritten (tests/e2e-loop.test.sh:139-143, tests/lib/run_project_turns.py:90-92 write authored details); tests/autopilot.test.sh, tests/autopilot-loop.test.sh (its wake assertion at tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py:216-222 uses assertIn on "T-001 ready: merge card details needed", and that prefix stays), tests/autopilot-jobs.test.sh keep their merge-card cases; tests/decide.test.sh merge validation; tests/lib/autopilot_task_resolution.py gains the draft wake identities named in Change 2.

Callers, all listed. merge_card is called only from job_completed at bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:445. advance at :240 is called from pull at bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:463, which the poll loop calls at :563. The draft branch at :286 is the only draft check on the advancement path; bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:500 and :513 check drafts only for branch updates and are unchanged. Merge-card details are read by fm-decide.sh --request (design :430-438) and by the autopilot at :503; the built path is new and read only by the same merge_card call.

Migration. No stored format changes. Authored decision-details files keep priority. The new state/decision-details-built/ directory holds autopilot-built files only. Each open draft pull request gets one wake on the first poll after upgrade.

Docs, edited in place. design/design.md §5.2 ("Captain decisions", the merge-card details paragraph at :449-455: for the self project the autopilot builds details from the answered dispatch card when none are authored, into state/decision-details-built/); §15.8 sub-heading "Autopilot owns PR advancement (T-175)" at :5791: the sentence "requests a card only from firstmate-authored details" (:5803-5804) and "Missing details queues one wake" (:5807) are updated for built details and the external case, and the draft wake is added; skills/firstmate/SKILL.md :228-238 (the wake list including missing merge-card details) and :916-926: firstmate no longer runs a merge path by hand and authors details only when the autopilot's wake asks; docs/verification/supervision.md :50-53: the wake kinds gain the draft wake and the missing-details wording names the build fallback.

intent.text: For the self project, the autopilot builds the merge card details from the answered dispatch card.
A draft pull request wakes firstmate once instead of stopping the merge path without a word.

why.text: The captain answered on 2026-10-07: "好 先B再C 其他照你的意思改".
Firstmate ran the merge path by hand with untracked scripts, and they failed in several ways.

scope_in: bin/lib/fm_merge_details.py: details from the dispatch card
bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py: details and the draft wake
scope_out: The gates and the merge lock

done.text: Intent 1: the autopilot writes checked details outside the gated inputs when none are authored. Test cases 1 to 8 prove it.
Intent 2: the autopilot wakes once for each draft head. Test case 9 proves it.

notes.text: Firstmate removes its local hand scripts after this task merges.
